body:
Repair human-step filing so a lane cannot re-file a human step Nate closed as not planned and re-block the ticket he unblocked, and so agent-doable work never rides inside a human step.

What it does:
- Before filing a Needs:human sub-issue that would block its parent ticket, read from GitHub the same parent's Needs:human sub-issues closed as not planned, compare the requested human-only action against each, and on a same-action match refuse the new filing or route it to review instead of filing it as a blocking human step.
- Split mixed filings: a request containing a human-only action plus agent-doable work files the agent-doable part as a separate Needs:agent ticket; the human step carries only the human-only action.
- Leave a record of a refused/routed repeat on the parent or attempted filing so the next run does not retry the same filing.

Ticketable acceptance:
- Replaying the Fantasy-GM sequence from the idea (#329 closed not planned, then #336 asking the same probe plus a docs sentence) does not re-block #312; the probe repeat is refused/routed and the docs sentence files as Needs:agent.
- Unit tests against fixtures cover a same-action repeat, a different-action non-repeat, and a mixed human-plus-agent filing.
- Verification runs the canonical test command `python3 -m pytest`.

Rejected:
- Fixing only the review trigger (the unsure inferred-premise reject and missing-sentence reject on PR #320): removes one trigger but leaves the refiling path open, so the guard is still required.
- A local cache, journal, or denylist of closed human steps: violates GitHub-is-state; the sibling set is derived from GitHub on each filing.
- A new label for repeat human steps: the label set is closed at needs-shaping and blocked without a plan.md change, and Needs:human plus closed not planned already encodes the state.
- Auto-reopening the closed-not-planned sibling or silently dropping the repeat: reopening overrides Nate's close, and a silent drop leaves no record to stop the next run retrying.
- Keeping agent-doable sentences inside the human ticket: Needs routes the owner, so agent work inside Needs:human waits in Nate's queue instead of running as agent work.

- Run the check in the shared filing path immediately before creating any blocking Needs:human sub-issue, reading siblings from GitHub. (rejected: Let each lane implement the repeat check from prose in its own prompt.; Two vendors implementing from prose drift silently, so the shared program must own the transition.)
- Match only on the same parent when the sibling is Needs:human closed not planned and the requested human-only action names the same operation on the same resource. (rejected: Treat any closed human step with overlapping wording as a repeat.; A narrow same-parent same-operation rule stops the #329/#336 repeat without blocking legitimate new human steps.)
- Hard-refuse the blocking filing and post a parent-issue comment citing the closed-not-planned sibling and requested action. (rejected: Route the repeat to review as a non-blocking ticket for a second look.; Nate already closed the action as not planned, so re-queueing wastes his throughput and risks re-blocking the ticket he unblocked.)

## What it is
Ticket 1 — Record the real implement launch path: read codex_run.py sandbox and network settings and one live command-center-tickets automation.toml with its prompt, recording which file was read; record which process launches the model shell, which runner calls must keep working from that shell (begin, finish-ticket), and which Codex app-level settings would also affect non-implement use; post the record on the parent issue; no behaviour change.
Ticket 2 — Compare viable levers on their merits and file build follow-ups: document the observed jeffy separate-user setup as readable without admin work, Codex app sandbox tightening with its app-wide blast radius, and moving runner git and gh calls out of the model shell, and GitHub branch rules requiring a pull request to update `main` in each member repo (command-center's `main` had no protection and no rulesets on 2026-09-27; record which member repos' plans allow branch rules, and whether a rule breaks `funnel merge`); record credential separation, durability effect, and admin cost for each; a lever is viable when it would stop model-shell gh and push while keeping begin and finish-ticket working; post the comparison on the parent issue and file each viable build as a new Ideas item linking back; no behaviour change, findings in GitHub only, no local state.

## Rejected
- PATH-scoped gh and funnel refuse plus git push allowlist around a Command Center-owned implement subprocess: cannot be built, falsified twice by direct observation on 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-25 that the Codex app launches the session and Command Center owns no subprocess to wrap, and refuse-outright would block the automation's own required begin and finish-ticket calls from the same shell.
- Refusal-count tripwire gating isolation behind a threshold: the counter cannot observe absolute-path gh bypass pinned as known non-interception, so zero refusals is consistent with full exposure; per the 2026-09-25 correction isolation is compared on merits, not deferred behind this count.
- Building separate-user isolation now without launch-path evidence: premature while Codex app-level effects and runner-call placement are unverified; the jeffy precedent is input to the comparison, not a build order.
- Hardening scripts/muse-implement: retired since 2026-09-22 while Codex implements both tiers, so it guards no live session.
- Env-strip of GH_TOKEN and finish-only push rights: env-strip removes nothing because keyring auth and SSH push do not read it, and finish-only breaks mid-run durability.
- Checked-in shims, logs, or absolute Mac paths, local-only or comment-scattered counts, and historical backfill: leak layout, break checkouts, violate GitHub-is-state, go stale or unsummable, and no refusal record exists to backfill.
- Broken or Maintenance class: no incident, no failing lane, and no known expiry date.

body:
Review judges each requirement literally against the diff with no handling for recorded departures, so a PR that lists a justified departure in its body Departures section is rejected for that departure on every review.

What this changes:
- Parse the PR body Departures section in the review path and make each entry available during requirement evaluation alongside the diff and ticket text.
- Apply the settled departure handling to departed requirements instead of marking them unmet, preserving the departure text and reason in the verdict record.
- Cover the two observed cases from PR #1649: the shaped allowlist entry and reconcile parity on the fixture pinning the 7-day anchor window.
- Add unit tests for parsing and verdict handling including malformed entries, plus a regression replay using the recorded #1649 packet.
- Acceptance: a re-review of the same diff and body no longer lists a recorded departure verbatim as blocking requirement unmet.

Rejected:
- Requiring a ticket-text edit for every wording slip: leaves any slightly wrong text deadlocking in review on the begin path.
- Removing departures from the implementer answer and PR body: deletes the reasoned signal instead of making review read it.
- Treating any Departures text as automatically satisfied without reason or evidence: weakens the review bar that checks diff against plan.
- Relying on watch-posted prose to clear a departure: the 05:46Z prose was already ignored by the 06:37Z verdict, so prose alone does not clear it.
- Deferring to #1626: that covers post-deploy evidence for an inferred premise proved by a later sibling ticket, not a departure recorded in the PR body.

- Well-formed means the entry names the departed requirement plus a non-empty reason, and malformed or reasonless entries are ignored so the requirement is judged literally. (rejected: Accept any Departures text including bare names or empty reasons as clearing the requirement.; Requiring name plus reason keeps the diff-against-plan bar fail-closed while preserving the implementer reasoned signal for judges.)

(rejected: Let each judge re-parse the body independently or hide raw departure text from judges behind the lister summary.; Single parse with shared presentation keeps lister and judges consistent and honors the fresh-read re-review rule without cross-stage drift.)

(rejected: Watch-posted departure prose counts alongside the PR body Departures section.; Technical default picks one canonical source, the PR body written by the implementer, and the 05:46Z prose already proved ignorable at 06:37Z.)

(rejected: Ship only unit tests with no replay of the recorded #1649 packet.; Replay proves the observed 05:01Z and 06:37Z failures no longer block while unit tests pin parsing and malformed handling, consistent with #1194 replay direction.)
